title: The model menu grew—and got clearer
summary:
More ways to use the text API arrived alongside repairs to caching, model discovery, documentation, and the community directory.

The text API added `openai-fast` for GPT-4.1-nano, `openai-roblox` for GPT-4.1-mini, and two rather different personas: Mirexa for in-character chat and image prompts, and Bidara for biomimicry design. The `openai` alias now points to GPT-4.1-mini; model metadata gained a tool-support flag, while several listings and routing mappings were tidied up. More choice is useful when the menu tells you what you’re choosing.

Completed streaming responses can be cached for reuse, with equivalent requests sharing keys across hosts and header handling avoiding double compression. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint also preserves supplied JSON Schemas by forwarding the full `response_format` object. A new websim Worker takes a URL prompt and returns a self-contained HTML page directly.

Polynate, Pollinations Task Master, Define, Rizqi O Chatbot, KoboldAI, Aiphoto智能绘画, and SingodiyaTech joined the project listings. They span audio, definitions, writing, image generation, and developer tooling—a useful reminder that one API rarely stays one kind of app.

The model list stopped advertising `llama-vision`, and listings for Phi-4 Instruct and Mirexa were clarified. MCP guides now distinguish the official server from the community-maintained MCPollinations server. Text-to-speech POST examples now show how to decode the base64 audio returned in JSON.
